visual: Rounded evergreen shrub · brilliant golden-yellow aromatic leaves · clusters of fragrant white star-shaped flowers
water: Water regularly while establishing; once established tolerates some drought. Avoid prolonged waterlogging.
soilWarning: No standing wet; exposed sites scorch it
prune: Pruning group 8; lightly shape after flowering and remove damaged or congested shoots.
toxicity: No known hazard; no significant toxicity commonly reported.
cvs: Sundance is the trade name associated with 'Lich'; synonyms include 'Brica' and 'Moonsleeper'.
hardinessNote: H4 · hardy through most of the UK, approximately −10 to −5°C
resilience: Evergreen and drought tolerant once established; reasonably robust in a sheltered, freely drained position.
uses: Shrub borders · evergreen structure · scented gardens · courtyards · informal hedging · containers

visual: Fast-growing arching shrub · sea-green stems · white hanging flowers enclosed by wine-red to purple bracts · dark purple berries
water: Keep moderately moist while establishing; established plants tolerate short dry periods.
prune: Pruning group 6 in early spring for vigorous new stems, or group 3 after flowering where a larger framework is wanted.
toxicity: Fruit is ornamental and should not be eaten; RHS advises gloves when handling.
hardinessNote: H5 · hardy in most UK locations, approximately −15 to −10°C
resilience: Very vigorous and adaptable; usually pest-free and can regenerate strongly after pruning.
uses: Woodland-style planting · wildlife gardens · informal borders · screening · bird-friendly planting

visual: Lax evergreen shrub · green leaves irregularly variegated cream-white · saucer-shaped purple flowers with vivid yellow centres
water: Keep evenly moist during active growth but ensure excess water drains freely; reduce watering in winter.
soilWarning: Shelter; cold exposed sites need protection
prune: Pruning group 9 if freestanding or group 12 when trained as a wall shrub.
toxicity: Harmful if eaten: all parts can cause severe discomfort; wear gloves when handling.
hardinessNote: H3 · hardy mainly in mild coastal or sheltered UK locations, approximately −5 to 1°C
resilience: Long flowering and vigorous in warmth but vulnerable to hard frost; performs best against a warm wall or under protection.
uses: Patio containers · conservatories · warm walls · Mediterranean planting · summer flowering displays
uncertain: RHS currently marks the cultivar name status as unresolved, although 'Variegata' is widely used horticulturally.

visual: Upright annual · creamy-white to pale yellow hibiscus flowers · striking dark purplish-maroon central eye · inflated seed capsules
water: Water moderately during active growth, allowing the surface to begin drying between waterings.
soilWarning: No cold wet soil; plant out after last frost
prune: No pruning required; deadhead if seed production is not wanted.
toxicity: No known hazard; no significant toxicity warning listed by RHS.
hardinessNote: H2 · tolerates cool conditions but not freezing; normally treated as an annual in the UK
resilience: Fast-growing annual in warm conditions but frost tender.
uses: Annual borders · cottage gardens · containers · subtropical-style planting · unusual flowering displays

visual: Large herbaceous perennial · stout reddish-purple stems · long racemes of small white-green flowers · glossy purple-black berries
water: Prefers consistent moderate moisture but established plants tolerate short dry periods.
prune: Cut dead top growth back after dormancy; remove spent fruiting stems earlier if self-seeding is undesirable.
toxicity: TOXIC if eaten. All parts are poisonous to people and pets; gloves are advisable because compounds can also be absorbed through damaged skin.
hardinessNote: Very cold-tolerant temperate perennial; underground crown survives winters far colder than typical lowland UK conditions.
resilience: Extremely vigorous, fast-growing and adaptable; resists many pests and can become difficult to eradicate once established.
uses: Wildlife planting · naturalistic planting · dramatic foliage and berries · large informal gardens
uncertain: RHS does not currently provide a readily retrievable species-level hardiness profile for Phytolacca americana; the H6-equivalent rating is inferred from its established temperate North American range and winter survival.

visual: Large architectural succulent · rigid grey-green sword-shaped leaves broadly edged yellow · formidable marginal and terminal spines
water: Water sparingly and allow the growing medium to dry well between waterings; keep much drier in winter.
soilWarning: Cold and winter wet kill it; drain sharply
prune: No pruning required; remove only dead or damaged leaves with appropriate protection.
toxicity: Sap is a skin irritant and the plant is harmful to dogs and cats if eaten; sharp marginal and terminal spines are an additional physical hazard.
hardinessNote: H2 · does not tolerate freezing reliably and requires winter protection in most of the UK
resilience: Exceptionally drought resistant and heat tolerant, but poor tolerance of frost and prolonged winter moisture.
uses: Architectural containers · Mediterranean gardens · conservatories · gravel gardens · summer patio displays

visual: Vigorous broad deciduous maple · unusual pinnate ash-like leaves · green young shoots · yellow autumn foliage · winged fruits on female trees
water: Water regularly while young; established trees prefer moderate moisture and tolerate ordinary well-drained garden conditions.
soilWarning: Needs a lot of room; no waterlogged ground
prune: Pruning group 1; minimal pruning, preferably undertaken during dormancy to remove damaged or poorly positioned branches.
toxicity: No major human toxicity warning from RHS; seeds and seedlings of box elder are associated with atypical myopathy in horses.
hardinessNote: H6 · hardy throughout the UK and northern Europe, approximately −20 to −15°C
resilience: Fast-growing, cold hardy and adaptable to a wide range of soils and light levels.
uses: Large gardens · specimen tree · informal landscapes · shade tree · autumn colour

visual: Compact aromatic evergreen lavender · variegated grey-green foliage with cream to yellow margins · fragrant blue to violet-blue flower spikes
water: Water while establishing then sparingly; allow soil to dry between waterings and keep comparatively dry through winter.
soilWarning: No heavy wet soil; keep mulch off the crown
prune: Pruning group 10; trim after flowering to maintain a compact shape but avoid cutting into old leafless wood.
toxicity: No known hazard as a garden plant; ingestion of concentrated aromatic oils can cause problems.
cvs: Possible identity is Lavandula angustifolia 'Platinum Blonde' ('Momparler') or Lavandula × intermedia 'Walberton's Silver Edge' ('Walvera').
hardinessNote: Both candidate cultivars are RHS H5, approximately −15 to −10°C, provided drainage is good.
resilience: Drought resistant and cold hardy when established in free-draining soil; winter wet is a greater risk than cold alone.
uses: Containers · edging · gravel gardens · wildlife gardens · Mediterranean planting · scented gardens
uncertain: Exact cultivar remains unresolved from the supplied name alone.
Lavandula angustifolia 'Platinum Blonde' has narrow grey-green leaves with creamy-yellow margins and is typically more compact.
Lavandula × intermedia 'Walberton's Silver Edge' has broader grey-green leaves edged cream and generally develops a broader plant.
